findings.text: §9 clause (2) closes on the read's first call "from the pinned cache" and on "§4's H200 fills at 132, 300 and 550 cells complete", but §4 node (a) (plan.html:74) is the step that "first adds that read at 132, 300 and 550 cells to the programs the pre-warm compiles into the pinned cache", and plan-section-depends-on declares s4 depends on s9 (plan.html:23), so §9 cannot measure what it names until §4 has run while §4 is ordered after §9

findings.reason: a worker cannot tell whether a peak above 120 GB is carried as a recorded value or fails the node, so the clause closes on neither reading and the 2026-11-18 unbounded-cold-compile ruling is restated as a bound in the very sentence that disclaims one.
findings.text: clause (2) says the 132-cell read's cold compile "completes inside one 120 GB CPU allocation, with its peak ... recorded and no bound on it"; a compile that exceeds 120 GB is killed by the allocation and fails the clause, so 120 GB is a peak-memory bound in effect while the same sentence says none exists, and §8 (plan.html:90) records that the read's current Hessian call already exceeds 120 GB, making it the binding number rather than a recorded observation
